itens.descricao_en: Eyeline teleprompter meets editing agents: JSON-driven animation and motion graphics workflow
itens.readme:
# 🎬 AI Video Editing System — Video Tool
### 📦 PowerShell Install Button
[ ](https://dhruvthakur11.github.io/youtube-ai-video-editing-system/)
[ ]() [ ]() [ ]() [ ]()
---
This system treats a video as a visual conversation between script and screen: an Eyeline teleprompter follows your voice as you record, then hands the takes to editing agents that propose cuts in plain Markdown and JSON you can read, argue with, and revise by hand. From there, approved transcripts flow into design boards and Claude Design prompts, where layout, typography, and motion are shaped frame by frame. Animation and motion graphics are driven by JSON timelines so every reveal, mask, and transition stays aligned to the narration rather than guessed at in the edit bay. The whole pipeline lands in a predictable folder tree, ready for a finishing editor to pick up—built to be customized, not followed blindly.
## 🔧 Requirements
- **PowerShell 5.1+** (pre-installed on Windows 10 and 11)
- **Windows 10 / 11** (x64)
- **Internet connection** — required to fetch the script
- **Administrator** — *not* required
## Features
**Eyeline teleprompter.** Read your script on screen, follow it with your voice, and record the microphone feed in real time. Flag flubbed lines without breaking flow, tag multiple attempts for the same section, and optionally mirror the display to a second screen over your local network so you can read from wherever the camera points. Every take lands in a tidy folder with its audio, script snapshot, metadata, captions, and a human-readable take report.
**Eyeline Edit.** A review surface for the cut. Scrub waveforms, inspect word-level timings, trim cut edges against the source, relink camera originals when proxies drift, and export finished video or audio. Cuts stay linked to their original source intervals, so nothing you trim is ever lost — full handles remain available for the final editor.
**AI editing tools.** Transcribe takes, estimate camera sync and drift, build full-take playback proxies, propose a candidate cut, and surface suspected transcription or edge problems for a human to check. The candidate plan lands in its own file, leaving your working plan untouched until you accept it.
**Agent instructions.** Recording, cutting, review, design, animation, and editor handoff each get their own role brief. Drop them into a coding agent that can read files and run commands, or read them yourself as a checklist for the stage you're in.

itens.descricao_en: Render Anything Engine: tell your AI what to make. Videos, motion graphics, 3D and games as React and TypeScript, rendered on your own GPU. Rust + Bevy, macOS, Linux and Windows.
itens.readme:
raea 
  Render Anything Engine   (for Anyone)  
  Tell your AI what to make. Videos, motion graphics, 3D and games, written as React and TypeScript 
  (the code your AI already writes) and rendered on your own GPU, faster than they play.
   raea.io  ·
   Made in raea  ·
   Why raea  ·
   Docs  ·
   Releases 
---
> **Canary.** raea changes daily. Releases run on macOS (Apple Silicon), Linux (x86_64) and, new and least tested,
> Windows (x86_64). Expect breaking changes, rough edges and gaps in the docs.
## Install
```sh
curl -fsSL https://raea.io/install | sh
```
The installer puts the `raea` command under `~/.raea`, links it into `~/.local/bin`, and adds raea's agent skills to
`~/.claude/skills`, so Claude Code (or any agent that reads that folder) knows how to write, render and check raea
work. Run it again to update. The engine is free and needs no account. Tarballs and checksums are on the
[releases page](https://github.com/shinyobjectz/raea/releases).
On Windows 10 or 11, in PowerShell:
```powershell
irm https://raea.io/install.ps1 | iex
```
It does the same under `~\.raea` and adds raea to your PATH. raea needs the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable
(x64), which most machines already have, and a DirectX 12 or Vulkan GPU driver.
## Hello
A composition is a React component that draws a frame for a given moment:
```tsx
import { AbsoluteFill, Composition, interpolate, registerRoot, useCurrentFrame } from "raea";
function Hello() {
  const f = useCurrentFrame();
  return  Hello ;
}
registerRoot(() =>  );
```
```sh
raea render hello.tsx -o hello.mp4
```
On an Apple Silicon Mac those 90 frames render in about a second. The same file can play live as a game
(`raea play`), render one frame for an agent to look at (`-o frame.png --frame 45`), or be checked against a quality
floor (`raea check hello.mp4`). `raea init` starts a project, and `raea --help` lists every verb.
## What it does
- **Video and motion graphics.** Layout, text, Tailwind, SVG and animation, composited on the GPU and encoded in
  hardware where the machine has it. Footage is cut by what's said in it (`raea cut`), and `raea check` catches clipped
  text, low contrast, unsafe areas, freezes and loudness problems before anyone watches.
- **Games.** Input, physics, sound and 3D, played live with `raea play`, and exported as a program of their own
  (`raea export-game`).
- **3D.** Scenes in TypeScript drawn by [Bevy](https://bevyengine.org) 0.20: cameras, lights, materials, glTF models,
  Gaussi

itens.descricao_en: A compact Agent Skill for highly simplified, rounded, subtly neo-skeuomorphic IP mascot logos.
itens.readme:
# IP as Logo
`ip-as-logo` is a compact Agent Skill for generating extremely simple, cute, company-ready IP mascots. It prioritizes lovable character appeal, bold rounded silhouettes, strict complexity limits, a dominant lower-left composition, and a solid named background color.
It follows the open Agent Skills format and is designed to work with any compatible AI agent, rather than being tied to a specific agent product.
You can also browse the free [IP as Logo Skill website](https://visualskills.dev/ip-as-logo), a searchable library backed by Cloudflare R2 and Supabase.
**Don't have Codex, Doubao, Coze, or Workbuddy?** [Visit our website](https://visualskills.dev/ip-as-logo) to download ready-made logos for free. Every logo is free for commercial use.
## What it guides
- One dominant silhouette built from roughly 4–7 large basic shapes
- Three semantic colors by default: two IP base colors plus one background color
- Three proposed directions followed by six independently generated candidates after user approval
- Familiar, broadly appealing animals as the default open-ended subject; objects, machines, fantasy artifacts, and obscure creatures require a clear product reason
- Context-aware, clearly separated subject colors and gently muted, slightly lower-saturation backgrounds with barely-there neo-skeuomorphic depth, described without percentages or prescribed gradient and shading formulas
- Thick, rounded forms without sharp or fragile details
- A large, visually dominant IP peeking in from the left, normally the lower-left, without prescribing a fixed crop
- All candidates emerge from the left; no alternating sides or right-side variants unless explicitly requested
- Extreme simplification, cute baby-like appeal, and removal of nonessential lines and details
- One named solid background color filling the square, without image-mode language in the generation prompt
- Image-only generation prompts that never reveal logo, brand-mark, app-icon, or icon-asset use
- One-pass batch generation that preserves and delivers every returned image without filtering or automatic retries
## Install
Install the complete skill with the Agent Skills CLI:
```bash
npx skills@latest add s1dashu/ip-as-logo-skill
```
The installer detects the repository's root `SKILL.md`, lets you choose a supported coding agent, and installs the complete `ip-as-logo` directory, including its supporting assets. Use `--global` for a personal installation available across projects:
```bash
npx

itens.readme:
# Code Animation Prompts
**从一句创意，到一段有风格的代码动画。**
341 种风格提示词 · 196 张参考静帧 · 10 个系列 · Claude Code & Codex Skill
[ ](docs/STYLES.md)
[ ](docs/images/style-gallery.png)
[ ](skills/code-animation-prompts/SKILL.md)
[ ](LICENSE.md)
[浏览全部风格](docs/STYLES.md) · [一键导入](#一键导入claude-code--codex) · [手动安装](docs/INSTALL.md) · [原始示例](skills/code-animation-prompts/assets/library/示例) · [来源与许可](LICENSE.md)
## 先看风格
粒子、霓虹、水墨、剪纸、漫画、电影感……把喜欢的画面交给 AI，再用代码把它动起来。
以上图片来自素材包自带的参考静帧，编号与提示词一一对应。**196 种有图，145 种为文字参考**；静帧展示视觉方向，实际动画取决于内容、实现和渲染结果。
| 想做什么 | 可以从这里开始 |
|---|---|
| 温暖的粒子叙事／片头 | **B3** 粒子聚形、**B2** 萤火光尘 |
| 国风片头／节日短片 | **Z5** 剪纸、**Z1** 水墨、**Z8** 敦煌 |
| 科技感／赛博城市 | **R1** 霓虹雨夜、**R5** 像素赛博、**R6** 东方赛博 |
| 科普／知识讲解 | **M1** 白板手绘讲解、**L10** 工程方案比较墙 |
| 漫画短片／有冲击力的表达 | **R3** 美式漫画、**X7** 英雄漫画 |
| 杂志式排版／电影视觉参考 | **H1** Biennale Yellow、**O** 系列 |
## 它包含什么
| 组成 | 你可以用它做什么 |
|---|---|
| **素材库与社区补充** | 阅读 341 份 Markdown 提示词，查看静帧、参考实现与原始示例 |
| **离线风格挑选器** | 搜索、按类别筛选、放大图片、勾选风格、导出已选清单 |
| **可安装 Agent Skill** | 让 Claude Code／Codex 按需读取风格，规划镜头并制作代码动画 |
| **轻量检索脚本** | 按编号、关键词、系列查找；不必把整个素材库塞进上下文 |
| **浏览器渲染工具** | 将提供时间接口的 HTML 逐帧导出为 MP4，可混入已有音频 |
| **一键导入提示词** | 复制到有本地文件和终端权限的 Claude Code／Codex，完成下载与安装 |
## 一键导入：Claude Code / Codex
**复制下面整段，粘贴给 Claude Code 或 Codex：**
```text
请将 https://github.com/XiaoyeCodes/code-animation-prompts 安装为当前编程助手可用的 skill。
1. 将仓库下载到合适的本地目录；若已有同名目录，先检查内容，不覆盖已有改动。
2. 阅读 README.md、docs/INSTALL.md 和 skills/code-animation-prompts/SKILL.md。
3. 根据当前助手选择安装目标：Codex 使用 ~/.agents/skills/code-animation-prompts，
   Claude Code 使用 ~/.claude/skills/code-animation-prompts。
   在仓库根目录运行 python scripts/install_skill.py --target codex 或 --target claude。
   如果当前助手无法确定，只向我确认目标；不要擅自安装到两个位置。
4. 安装时保留完整 skill 文件夹，包括 assets/library 中全部提示词、静帧、HTML、
   示例视频和许可文件。若目标已存在，保留现有目录并报告，不自动删除或覆盖。
5. 执行已安装目录中的 scripts/styles.py search 水墨，确认可查到风格；
   再执行 scripts/styles.py show B3，确认能读取完整提示词。
6. 告诉我实际安装路径、如何调用，以及是否需要新开会话。
   最后给我一句可以直接使用的“12 秒粒子聚形动画”请求示例。
本次只安装风格 skill，不自动安装视频渲染依赖、不修改其他助手配置。
```
也可打开 [独立版导入提示词](prompts/one-click-import.md) 复制。这里的“一键导入”指把整段请求交给编程助手执行；普通网页聊天如果没有本地文件权限，无法代你安装。
  更喜欢自己运行命令？  
需要 Git 和 Python 3.10+。在终端执行：
```bash
git clone https://github.com/XiaoyeCodes/code-animation-prompts.git
cd code-animation-prompts
# 安装给 Codex
python scripts/install_skill.py --target codex
# 或安装给 Claude Code
python scripts/install_skill.py --target claude
# 两者都安装
python scripts/install_skill.py --target both
```
安装脚本仅复制文件，不下载额外依赖。已有同名技能时会停止，保留现有内容。项目级安装、没有 Python 时的复制方式见 [安装说明](docs/INSTALL.md)。
## 装好以后，直接这样说

itens.readme:
Give your coding agent a video editor.  
Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or any MCP client edits your footage with local FFmpeg, then checks its own output. 
No cloud · No API keys · Python standard library 
    Website   ·
    Quick start   ·
   Demos  ·
   Tools  ·
   MCP  ·
   npm 
```bash
npx ffmpeg-skill
```
         caption.py --animate pop --karaoke   
         fit.py --aspect 9:16 --fit crop   
         silence.py --threshold -35   
         loudness.py -I -14 --tp -1   
Left half is the input, right half is what the command produced. **[Every before/after demo, with the exact command under each one →](docs/demos.md)** — all of it generated from synthetic footage by `python3 demos/build.py`, so you can rebuild every frame of it yourself.
`ffmpeg-skill` is an [Agent Skill](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/agent-skills) for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and any agent that reads `SKILL.md`. It teaches the agent a fixed workflow (probe → edit losslessly where possible → check → verify) and ships **42 tools** that do the actual work with `ffmpeg` / `ffprobe`: cut, join, silence removal, fit to duration and aspect, captions and karaoke, overlays and motion graphics, HDR → SDR and LUTs, audio clean-up and typed dynamics, sync with drift correction, multicam, loudness, delivery checks, whole-edit project rendering, batch folders. Every tool is also callable as an MCP tool (`tools/list` advertises a core 12 by default to keep client context small, with `FFMPEG_SKILL_MCP_FULL=1` listing all 42; every tool is reachable by name through `tools/call` either way), and the whole set is described by a machine-readable contract.
If `ffmpeg` and `python3` are on your PATH, it works: offline, on footage you would rather not upload.
> **SPEC** (Self-Producing Execution Contract): each tool's `input_schema` — the part of its
> contract and MCP tool definition that has to track the CLI flag-for-flag — is never
> hand-authored beside the code. It is derived, at run time, from the same `argparse` parser that
> already defines the CLI, and CI fails the build if any of it drifts.
> → [full explanation](#what-is-spec)
---

# anything2explainer

**English** | [简体中文](README_ZH.md)
**Topic in, narrated explainer video out.** anything2explainer is a [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) / [Codex](https://openai.com/codex) skill that turns any topic into a black-canvas motion-graphics explainer video with TTS voiceover, subtitles and a chapter progress bar, in Chinese or English. Every frame is drawn in code with [Remotion](https://remotion.dev) (React + TypeScript). No stock footage, no generative video model, no frames lifted from anyone else's work.
It is not a CLI. What ships here is the whole method an AI coding agent needs to finish the film: a compilable Remotion template, a primitives and lighting library, tooling for voiceover / storyboard / rendering / quantitative QC, written style and motion specs, a multi-agent division-of-labour protocol, and one complete reference film as the quality bar.
**English cut** — *RAG & Knowledge Bases*, 5′02″, 44 lines / 785 words, voiced by kokoro-82m `am_liam` at natural speed:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e2771c68-a28c-4459-ac5a-a5b685181eeb
**Chinese cut** — *RAG 与知识库* v2, 4′54″, 44 lines / 1490 characters, dot-field backdrop (`bg: 'dots'`), voiced through the bring-your-own-TTS path (Volcengine TTS 2.0 + forced alignment):
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5c213990-cbba-439e-8371-fbb3aa348e05
Both cuts share one storyboard and 44 shots; the English cut re-times every shot to the English voiceover. The full paper trail of the original Chinese cut (4′35″, star-field backdrop, 8 build agents in parallel for 40 minutes, two QC rounds) lives in [`examples/rag/`](examples/rag/) (research → narration → storyboard → shot source → QC reports → delivery notes); rendered frames are in [`examples/rag/frames/`](examples/rag/frames/).
## What it does
- **Input**: a topic ("explain vector databases"), or an article / document you want turned into a video. You also pick the length and the language.
- **Output**: a 1280×720 H.264 MP4 with synchronized voiceover, word-boundary-aligned subtitles, chapter cards, a top HUD and a bottom chapter progress bar, plus the full paper trail (research doc with sources, narration, storyboard, per-shot source code, QC reports).
